summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, type 1 diabetes, bipolar disorder, and PTSD was admitted for a scheduled ERCP to remove a pancreatic stent. During the procedure, a stricture in the pancreatic duct and multiple stones were found. The stricture was dilated with a balloon, stones were removed, and a new stent was placed. The patient experienced post-procedural abdominal pain and a history of hypoglycemic episodes, which were managed with adjusted insulin dosing and pain control. He was monitored for stability, advanced to a full diet, and discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with his primary care provider and return in eight weeks for stent removal.
